Maya Patel: Quick design q: split button vs single CTA in dense table rows — what should primary look like? Samir Chen: I lean split for actions where dropdown has destructive options. Keeps primary action visible. But visual density might suffer in compact table. Diego Torres: Agree. Maybe we collapse to icon-only primary at <3 columns? or use hover reveal? Anika Rao: Hover reveals are bad for accessibility. Keyboard users won't discover it. :warning: Maya Patel: Good call. What about making the primary full-width but use a micro secondary chevron? Example: https://figma.redwood/mock123 (mock) Samir Chen: Visuals: primary solid 32px, secondary chevron 24px. Spacing token between them seems too big — current token 'gap-xs' feels like 12px, we want 6px. Diego Torres: That suggests we need a smaller token. Proposal: rename 'gap-xs' -> 'gap-xxs' and set to 6px. Anyone opposed? Anika Rao: Love rename for clarity. Also add a note in tokens doc: 'do not use for list dividers' — many devs misuse it. DesignBot: Automated a11y scan: split-button label missing aria-expanded on menu button in mock. Fails WCAG 2.1 A. Maya Patel: Thanks bot. I'll add aria-expanded and aria-controls. For toasts: placement overlapping pinned filters on dashboard — can we move to top-right or make toasts respect container padding? Samir Chen: Top-right is safer for charts, but in RTL locales that'll be top-left. Need mirrored placement config. Also ensure aria-live=polite on non-critical toasts. Diego Torres: Edge case: long toasts break the table header when they push content. Suggest toast max-width 420px and truncation with expand link. Anika Rao: Keyboard: toast should be dismissable via Escape when focused, and focus should return to previously focused element. Maya Patel: I'll update the component spec and add small code sample: `````
````` Samir Chen: :thumbsup: Add unit tests for spacing tokens and a11y hooks. I'll pick this up. DesignBot: Noted. Created ticket #UI-4227 for split-button updates, #UI-4228 for toast positioning and tokens. Maya Patel: Sweet. I'll push a PR by EOD with visuals and spec copy. Thanks team!
